measured_priors_additions.sample: Laboratory studies plus Billboard Hot 100 data from 1958-2012
measured_priors_additions.finding: Greater lyrical repetition increased processing fluency and was associated with broader/faster marketplace adoption, but too much word repetition could weaken the benefit.
measured_priors_additions.use: Let the strongest hook phrase repeat enough to become familiar, but use micro-variation and avoid mindless over-repetition.
measured_priors_additions.source: Nunes, Ordanini & Valsesia, Journal of Consumer Psychology, 2015

measured_priors_additions.sample: Hundreds of thousands of English-language popular songs across five genres over five decades
measured_priors_additions.finding: Lyrics became simpler and more repetitive over time, with genre-specific differences; emotional language also became more negative and personal.
measured_priors_additions.use: Do not mistake complexity for quality. Match vocabulary and repetition to the song, while keeping emotional specificity and originality.
measured_priors_additions.source: Scientific Reports, 2024, 'Song lyrics have become simpler and more repetitive over the last five decades'

intro.goal: establish identity without explaining the whole song
rules: instrumental identity may be stronger than lyrics
do not repeat the hook's exact job

pre_hook.goal: create lift/tension or simplify before hook
rules: increase expectancy with repetition or rising contour
skip it if beat has no real lift
title phrase should sound natural aloud

post_hook.goal: extend hook energy without adding another verse
rules: fragment, ad-lib, or no vocal are valid

bridge.goal: change perspective, harmony, or emotional meaning
rules: contrast matters more than word count
one strong line can carry the section

outro.goal: leave a final emotional image or motif
rules: reprise, fragment, or silence are valid
do not explain the song after it is over

hook_archetypes.name: question-answer
hook_archetypes.best_when: song tension can be stated simply

hook_archetypes.name: mantra
hook_archetypes.shape: one phrase repeated with delivery/production progression
hook_archetypes.best_when: beat is hypnotic and phrase is strong enough

hook_archetypes.name: micro-variation
hook_archetypes.shape: same syntax repeated with one key word changed

hook_archetypes.name: two-line-loop
hook_archetypes.best_when: melody and production carry the hook

hook_archetypes.name: melodic-vowel
hook_archetypes.shape: short setup -> held vowel payoff -> instrumental answer
hook_archetypes.best_when: vocal tone is a major asset

hook_archetypes.name: call-response
hook_archetypes.best_when: production has room for layered vocals

hook_archetypes.name: payoff-line
hook_archetypes.shape: 2-3 setup cells -> one unforgettable final line

flow_archetypes.name: pocket-lock
flow_archetypes.description: repeat one rhythmic cell until it feels inevitable; change only after listener learns it

flow_archetypes.name: laid-back-behind-beat
flow_archetypes.description: enter slightly after expected pulse and use rests to create weight

flow_archetypes.name: front-loaded
flow_archetypes.description: cluster syllables early in phrase, then leave the end open

flow_archetypes.name: back-half-rush
flow_archetypes.description: start spacious and accelerate only at phrase ending

flow_archetypes.name: stair-step
flow_archetypes.description: repeat similar rhythm with one added/removed syllable each line

flow_archetypes.name: syncopated-bounce
flow_archetypes.description: alternate on-beat anchors with off-beat pickups

flow_archetypes.name: triplet-burst
flow_archetypes.description: use short triplet bursts as contrast, not the entire verse unless beat demands it

flow_archetypes.name: sung-tail
flow_archetypes.description: rap/speak the setup and sing/hold the last emotionally important word

flow_archetypes.name: boundary-switch
flow_archetypes.description: switch cadence at a 4/8-bar boundary, section change, drum fill, or melodic change

flow_archetypes.name: dropout-return
flow_archetypes.description: stop vocal for a beat/bar, then re-enter with same or slightly changed motif

rhyme_strategies.name: conversational-slant
rhyme_strategies.rule: natural speech first; slant rhyme is enough

rhyme_strategies.name: internal-cluster
rhyme_strategies.rule: cluster internal rhymes around meaning, not filler

rhyme_strategies.name: multisyllabic-chain
rhyme_strategies.rule: keep sentence meaning intact across the chain

rhyme_strategies.name: vowel-family
rhyme_strategies.rule: choose endings that sing comfortably even if spelling differs

rhyme_strategies.name: unrhymed-payoff
rhyme_strategies.rule: a strong unrhymed line can be better than a forced rhyme

rhyme_strategies.name: micro-rhyme
rhyme_strategies.rule: repeat short sound cells inside a phrase rather than forcing full end rhymes

melodic_space_rules: Silence is a compositional event, not missing content.
A strong 4-bar section may need only 1-2 lyric attacks.
Let held vowels, delay tails, ad-libs, and instrumental motifs occupy space.
When a phrase lands, test one full beat or bar of silence before adding another line.
Hooks usually need fewer unique words than verses.
If cutting 20-40% of the words improves melody, cut them.
Do not place a new sentence on every downbeat by default.
Use repeated fragments when a new sentence would only be filler.

emotional_arc_templates.name: memory-to-present
steps: final hook changed by present reality

narrative_devices: contrast between what narrator says and does
small event with large emotional consequence
anti_patterns: one lyric line per bar just because space exists
abstract emotion stacked without concrete detail
8 unique hook lines when 2-3 phrases would work
technical rhyme density in a section that should breathe
explaining the concept after the hook already communicated it
generic AI wording such as empty references to ghosts, darkness, demons, broken pieces, scars, or drowning unless a specific scene earns it
overusing timestamps, phone screens, empty rooms, rain, or highways as automatic emotional shorthand
forcing a title phrase that sounds unnatural in normal speech
holding notes simply because there is empty time

candidate_tournament.stage_1: Generate 3 distinct technique blends using beat evidence and reference profiles.
candidate_tournament.stage_2: Generate 5 short hook seeds with different rhythmic/emotional shapes; do not write full choruses yet.
candidate_tournament.stage_3: Score hook seeds for recall, natural speech, beat fit, vocal ease, emotional specificity, and originality.
candidate_tournament.stage_4: Keep top 2, rewrite each once to remove awkward/AI-sounding wording, then select one winner.
candidate_tournament.stage_5: Test 2 verse pockets against the winning hook: one simpler, one more rhythmically active.
candidate_tournament.stage_6: Write the full song only after the hook and verse pocket pass.
candidate_tournament.stage_7: Run speak-aloud, overfill, repetition, Verse-2-progression, and cliché checks.
candidate_tournament.stage_8: Cut anything that exists only to complete a rhyme or fill a bar.

personalization_schema.writing_samples: User-owned lyric samples used only to infer vocabulary, sentence length, directness, rhyme habits, and phrasing. Do not copy them verbatim unless user explicitly asks.
personalization_schema.dislikes: Patterns the user says felt weird, forced, wordy, generic, badly placed, or hard to perform.

song_record_schema.purpose: Future per-song structural analysis without storing lyrics or melodies.

selection_logic_v2.1: Start with beat evidence: structure, energy, drums, melodic openness, and vocal space.
selection_logic_v2.2: Choose relevant genre/era priors only as weak priors, never as commands.
selection_logic_v2.3: Select 3 technique blends and run candidate tournament.
selection_logic_v2.4: Apply personal writing DNA and accumulated feedback before finalizing.
selection_logic_v2.5: Prefer natural phrasing and beat fit over technical complexity.
selection_logic_v2.6: Keep hook simpler than verses and make Verse 2 add information.
selection_logic_v2.7: Use repetition when it increases recall; stop before it becomes empty repetition.
selection_logic_v2.8: Run an overfill cut and a cliché/AI-wording cut.
selection_logic_v2.9: Explain the winning technique blend in plain language, not artist imitation terms.
selection_logic_v2.10: No hit guarantee; output only diagnostic potential scores.

artist_profiles_additions.translation: Use fragments and repeated motifs when tone/groove can carry meaning.
Treat vocal production and negative space as composition without copying recognizable effects.
Keep verses readable, grounded, and meaning-first.
Use surprising structure only when it serves a clear concept.
Use a simple central thesis and let arrangement create scale; do not imitate lyrics or melodies.
Let rock dynamics amplify a concise chorus rather than adding more words.
Use clear role separation between rhythmic verse and melodic chorus when beat supports it.
Use theatrical structure only when the concept earns it; keep individual lines natural.
Allow imperfect sentence shapes and slant rhyme if they sound emotionally true.
Use concrete scenes and leave interpretive space instead of explaining everything.
